title: Bonds Almost Able to Break Even Thanks to Tech Turmoil
summary:
Bonds Almost Able to Break Even Thanks to Tech Turmoil 

             
             
            Tech stocks embarked on a wild ride starting with earnings releases after the bell yesterday. While today's recap title mentions "breaking even," if we were to measure today's bond market movement versus yesterday's 3pm ET levels, 10yr yields are more than 5bps lower. In other words, those earnings releases created a big late-day rally yesterday and today became largely about trying to hold onto the gains. By mid-day, bonds were a bit weaker with 10yr yields approaching 4.96%. Around 1240pm, news broke regarding Anthropic being unlikely to receive an "investment grade" rating after its IPO. This pushed the NASDAQ even deeper into negative territory and helped bonds make it most of the way back to "unchanged" by 3pm.

title: New Home Sales Reinforce Last Month's Rebound
summary:
New home sales lost almost no ground in September, effectively reinforcing the healthy rebound seen in August's report.   The Census Bureau's New Residential Construction report clocked sales at an annual pace of 676k, down only 0.6% month over month. As seen in the chart below, the broader trend has been sideways for nearly 3 years now.    The number of new houses for sale slipped to  476,000 , down 1.0% from August and 2.3% from a year earlier. With inventory edging lower alongside sales, the implied supply eased to  8.4 months , compared with 8.5 months in August and 8.2 months last September.  Prices rebounded from August's decline. The median sales price rose to  $400,400 , up 3.9% for the month but still 3.9% below September 2025. The average sales price increased 0.4% to  $472,800 , leaving it 6.7% below its year-ago level. As a reminder, these figures are broadly based and don't factor in location, lot size, and other key pricing components

title: Home Price Appreciation Edges Higher in August
summary: Home price appreciation picked up again in August (as reported this week), but the improvement was minimal.   The FHFA House Price Index rose  0.3%  from July to August, bringing annual appreciation to  2.4% . July's previously reported monthly gain was revised down from 0.3% to 0.2%. Regional results remained uneven, with annual appreciation ranging from 0.5% in the Mountain division to 4.4% in the East North Central division.  Case-Shiller's national index rose  2.1%  year over year, up from 1.9% in July. The 10-City Composite gained  3.6% , while the 20-City Composite rose  2.7% .    Even with the recent improvement, the inflation-adjusted trend remains negative. Consumer prices rose 3.4% annually in August, well above the 2.1% increase in national home prices. That gap has persisted for more than a year, offering some relief on a relative affordability basis even as elevated home prices and mortgage rates continue to challenge buyers.  Case-Shiller's metro-level results continued to show a sharp divide between markets. Chicago led the 20 tracked cities for the  sixth consecutive month , with prices up 6.7% year over year. New York followed at 6.2%, and Cleveland gained 4.3%. Seattle remained at the other end of the spectrum, with prices down  2.0%  annually, followed by Las Vegas at -1.3% and Denver at -0.8%. title: Mortgage Demand Bounces Back, Sort Of
summary:
Mortgage applications finally rebounded as mortgage rates fell for a second straight week. The Mortgage Bankers Association (MBA) reported a  3.4% increase  in total application volume for the week ending October 23.  The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate declined to  7.37%  from 7.41%, its lowest level in three weeks. Both purchase and refinance applications moved higher, but just barely, and well below levels from last year.  The seasonally adjusted Purchase Index rose  4%  for the week, and still  18% below year-ago levels . Refinances increased 3%, offering only a modest rebound from a market still  61% below  its level a year earlier.      “The decline in rates gave borrowers some relief, with applications rebounding slightly, particularly conventional applications,” said MBA's Joel Kan. He noted that mortgage rates remain more than a percentage point above year-ago levels, while most homeowners have little incentive to refinance. Adjustable-rate mortgages accounted for  11.3% of applications , the highest share in more than a year, as borrowers sought lower monthly payments.   Mortgage Rate Summary:

title: Mortgage Rates End Week at Lows
summary: The rate market continues taking cues from turmoil in the tech sector. That resulted in the lowest rates in more than a month today as tech stocks slide to their lowest levels since July.   The biggest shift for the underlying bond market (bonds dictate rates) came just before 1pm on reports that Anthropic's post IPO credit rating was not likely to be "investment grade." That matters because it means Anthropic would face higher borrowing costs.   Given the company's key role in driving the AI buildout, there are two implications that helped bonds/rates today. First, higher borrowing costs mean lower potential debt issuance, and that issuance has been a key factor in pushing interest rates higher in 2026. Second, any headwinds for major AI companies suggest potential economic headwinds given the central role AI plays in the current economic growth cycle. In general, lower/slower economic growth is good for rates/bonds, all else equal.   The average mortgage lender added modestly to yesterday's larger improvement, resulting in a top-tier 30yr fixed rate just under 7.30%. This is the lowest level since September 23rd, 2026.

title: Broker, DPA, AI Governance, Benchmark, U/W Products; Webinars; STRATMOR on Mergers
summary: As companies around the nation stage in-person or virtual costume contests, here’s some information for you a little off the beaten path. People want to own a home (“no one grows up wanting to be a renter”) regardless of… the amount of daylight? Looking at averages in the Continental United States (not Alaska or Hawaii), the difference between the amount of daylight on the first day of summer and the first day of winter is 5 ½ hours, “cushioned” by adjusting our timepieces. As much of the nation prepares to “fall back” this Sunday, talk again has come up about Congress eliminating this practice. Despite being passed in the House, and pressure from Donald Trump, several senators are holding up legislation that would eliminate changing the clocks. Supporters argue that ending the time change would mean less hassle and provide more daylight during the afternoon, when Americans are most active (except for me cuz that’s my nap time). Opponents say commuters in some states wouldn’t see the sun in winter until after 9 AM, and sunrise in the summer would be at 4 or 5 AM. Good luck with that one, Congress. title: Bond Yields Not Eager to Follow Stocks Lower
summary: Bonds were initially stronger in the overnight session with 10yr yields briefly falling under 4.90%. The rally generally aligned with overnight losses in the stock market, at least at first. When European markets came online, bonds began drifting more sideways even as stocks gradually declined to new lows. Given that today is month-end and that much of this month has seen quite a lot of volatility, it's reasonable to expect compulsory month-end trades to set the tone. Translation: bonds could do their own thing for their own reasons regardless of what's going on in stocks. Some analysts are reporting that month-end rebalancing models are calling for selling some bonds and buying some stocks, but we wouldn't lose sleep over that one unless stocks end up surging into positive territory.
